0.headline: Travomint parent SNVA Traveltech files UDRHP with SEBI for IPO; issue entirely an offer for sale
0.heading: Travomint parent SNVA Traveltech files UDRHP with SEBI for IPO; issue entirely an offer for sale
0.intro: Travomint IPO | The company plans to offer 12.75 crore equity shares through the IPO, comprising entirely an offer for sale.
0.body:
Uttar Pradesh-based SNVA Traveltech, the parent company of Travomint, an online travel booking platform, has filed an updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), taking another step towards its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The company plans to offer 12.75 crore equity shares through the IPO, comprising entirely an offer for sale (OFS), with no fresh issue component, according to the UDRHP filed on November 5.

Consequently, the net proceeds from the offer, excluding offer-related expenses, will go to the selling shareholders and promoters, Alok Kumar Singh and Vivek Kumar Singh.

SNVA Traveltech had initially filed its IPO papers with SEBI through the confidential filing route on April 1, 2026.

Established in 2017, the company operates an online travel platform primarily focused on air ticket bookings. Through its network of travel partners, it provides customers access to real-time inventory from airlines and hotels, enabling them to book flights, hotel stays and other travel-related services.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Financial Performance
According to the F&amp;S Report, SNVA Traveltech recorded a revenue CAGR of approximately 123.26 percent between FY24 and FY26, making it one of its strongest growth periods.

For the quarter ended June 2026, the company reported a consolidated profit of Rs 23.4 crore on revenue of Rs 51.2 crore.

For FY26, the company reported a consolidated profit of Rs 70.8 crore, registering a 73.7 percent increase from Rs 40.8 crore in the previous financial year.

Revenue from operations grew 58.1 percent to Rs 189.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 119.6 crore in FY25.

Equirus Capital and Anand Rathi Advisors have been appointed as the merchant bankers to manage the Travomint IPO.

1.headline: Anthropic IPO buyers see valuation down as low as $1.2 trillion
1.heading: Anthropic IPO buyers see valuation down as low as $1.2 trillion
1.intro: Anthropic's expected IPO valuation is facing fresh scrutiny after a sharp selloff in technology stocks. Prospective investors are discussing a valuation of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, down from earlier estimates of up to $2 trillion.
1.body:
Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering plans ran into a punishing post-election selloff, prompting a rethink among prospective investors of the company’s expected valuation.

Ahead of the AI lab kicking off formal IPO marketing next week, potential buyers are discussing a $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion valuation range for the company, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified as the information isn’t public.

Some investors weighing bids previously told bankers on the IPO that their estimate of a fair valuation had moved to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion, Bloomberg News has reported. That has shifted again after the Nasdaq 100 index plunged 6.4% on Thursday, wiping out $2.3 trillion in market value, a record for a single day.

Deliberations are ongoing and no final decisions have been made, the person said. A spokesperson for Anthropic declined to comment.

Volatile Environment

A volatile environment for tech stocks has already dented the outlook for what would be the first IPO by a so-called frontier AI model maker. Investors estimated a fair valuation for Anthropic as high as $2 trillion in early October, people familiar with the matter have said. The retreat to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion came after a company briefing on its latest financials in October, Bloomberg News reported at the time.

Questions about the Claude chatbot maker’s valuation in the IPO accelerated after the Democratic sweep of Congress triggered the prospect of greater scrutiny over the pace and impact of data center expansion. The Cboe Volatility Index rose to the highest since April 2025 on Thursday, making any IPO more difficult for investors to stomach.

“I would expect, based on the derating we saw in the AI space, valuations might need to be at least at the very low end of the rumored target range of $1.5 to $2 trillion, maybe some 10% to 15% below that,” said Stephan Kemper, chief investment officer at BNP Paribas Wealth Management Germany.

Michael Alfaro, the chief investment officer of Gallo Partners, a long-short and event-driven hedge fund, told Bloomberg News before Thursday’s market rout that Anthropic needed to target a valuation between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion “in order to build a quality book.”

“If they set a valuation toward the bottom of the range, say $1.2 trillion, they shouldn’t have a problem finding investors,” said David Rainville, a technology portfolio manager at Sycomore Asset Management.

Still, Max Kettner, chief multi-asset strategist at HSBC Holdings Plc, said around $1 trillion could be a more comfortable level for the valuation, reducing the risk of elevated volatility once trading begins.

“I don’t think we need the headline ‘oh my god, it is a trillion dollar IPO,’ because I think what’s actually more important is the secondary,” Kettner told Bloomberg Radio. “If we get a dynamic like we had with SpaceX, that you get it on secondary and then stock rips for a couple hours, but then it dumps, in the current environment you don’t want to have that.”

Anthropic and its selling shareholders may start the formal marketing with a conservative size and valuation target and increase it based on a positive initial response from investors. Chipmaker Cerebras Systems Inc. and design software firm Figma Inc. both sold more shares than they initially marketed as bankers gauged rising demand. However, both are now trading well below their IPO prices.

Another, less palatable option is for Anthropic to delay its plans. Companies have to have their IPO filings available to the public for at least 15 calendar days before they can begin formal marketing, typically followed by pricing and trading a week later, but some choose to wait weeks or even months after filing publicly to kick off marketing, updating additional quarterly financial data to keep their disclosures fresh.

“The selloff poses a slight risk for the Anthropic IPO, of course, but when you think of it, maybe it’s better to go to the market when the valuation excesses have already been purged,” said Alexandre Baradez, chief market analyst at IG in Paris.
1.ai_impact_text_summary_s: Anthropic's upcoming IPO valuation faces downward pressure, dropping to an estimated $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion amid a severe post-election tech stock selloff, regulatory concerns, and market volatility. While investors debate lower targets or potential delays, Anthropic could start conservatively.

2.headline: Quadria Capital-backed Encube Ethicals gets SEBI nod for Rs 3,000 crore IPO
2.heading: Quadria Capital-backed Encube Ethicals gets SEBI nod for Rs 3,000 crore IPO
2.intro: Under the OFS, the promoter plans to sell shares worth up to Rs 2,000 crore, while investor Frontier Investment Holdings, managed by Quadria Capital, intends to offload shares worth Rs 1,000 crore.
2.body:
Quadria Capital-backed pharmaceutical company Encube Ethicals has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to proceed with its initial public offering (IPO).

The company had filed its draft offer document with the capital markets regulator on August 1, 2026.

SEBI issued its observations on the company's draft papers on November 4, according to the processing status of draft offer documents published by the regulator on November 6.

The issuance of observations allows the company to proceed with its IPO plans by filing the red herring prospectus with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) and subsequently launching the public issue for subscription within the next 12 months.

Mumbai-headquartered Encube Ethicals proposes to raise Rs 3,000 crore through the IPO, comprising entirely an offer for sale (OFS), with no fresh issue component.

Under the OFS, the promoter plans to sell shares worth up to Rs 2,000 crore, while investor Frontier Investment Holdings, managed by Quadria Capital, intends to offload shares worth Rs 1,000 crore.

Frontier Investment Holdings held a 15.02 percent stake in the pharmaceutical company.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Promoted by Mehul Madhusudan Shah, Encube Ethicals operates two manufacturing facilities in Goa and Indore and has three business verticals: global generics, global contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO), and India-branded formulations.

The company had a total installed manufacturing capacity of 15,624 metric tonnes as of March 2026.

The company's financial performance has been robust in recent years. Its net profit grew 75 percent year-on-year to Rs 436.7 crore, while revenue increased 34.7 percent to Rs 1,848.7 crore compared with the previous year.

JM Financial, Axis Capital and Kotak Mahindra Capital Company are the merchant bankers managing the Encube Ethicals IPO.

Meanwhile, SEBI also issued observations on the draft IPO papers of four other companies — IFL Finance, Arjun Jewellers, Sagar Defence Engineering and Mahanadi Coalfields — on the same day.
